description.value: This study investigated the clinical and neural correlates of Time- and Event-based prospective memory disruption in Alzheimer's disease and behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia using whole-brain structural MRI and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: To investigate the clinical and neural correlates of Time- and Event-based PM disruption in AD and the behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD).

value: we predicted that unique neuroanatomical correlates of PM dysfunction would emerge in each patient group.

Specifically, we hypothesized that a distributed network of frontal, medial temporal, and parietal regions would be implicated in AD, whereas predominantly anteromedial temporal and prefrontal regions would be involved in bvFTD.
we predicted that the hippocampus would represent a common neural correlate across the two disease syndromes.

spans.text: Given converging evidence pointing to dissociable neural substrates of episodic memory disruption in AD versus bvFTD [6, 7], we predicted that unique neuroanatomical correlates of PM dysfunction would emerge in each patient group. Specifically, we hypothesized that a distributed network of frontal, medial temporal, and parietal regions would be implicated in AD, whereas predominantly anteromedial temporal and prefrontal regions would be involved in bvFTD.

value: BvFTD patients showed pronounced gray matter decreases in bilateral medial and lateral prefrontal regions, including the orbitofrontal and anterior cingulate cortices, extending into bilateral insular and lateral and medial temporal regions including the hippocampi; posterior regions including bilateral occipital cortices and the right angular and supramarginal gyri were also affected.

definition.value: Regions overlapping between AD and bvFTD associated with decreased gray matter intensity related to Time-based prospective memory performance.

value: Regions commonly implicated in Time-based PM disruption, irrespective of group, included the bilateral hippocampi, bilateral amygdalae, the left temporal pole, and left temporal fusiform cortex.

definition.value: Regions showing gray matter intensity decrease exclusive to AD associated with Time-based prospective memory performance.

value: A distributed network of regions was implicated in Time-based PM disruption in AD, including bilateral orbitofrontal cortices and frontal poles, bilateral temporal poles, bilateral hippocampi, bilateral occipital cortices, and the left angular gyrus.

definition.value: Regions showing gray matter intensity decrease exclusive to bvFTD associated with Time-based prospective memory performance.

value: Regions exclusively implicated for Time-based PM disruption in bvFTD were centered on the left frontal and left anteromedial temporal lobes, including the temporal fusiform cortex, temporal pole, hippocampus, and orbitofrontal cortex.

definition.value: Voxel-based morphometry results showing regions of significant gray matter intensity decrease associated with Event-based prospective memory performance; no significant clusters survived.

value: The overlap analysis failed to reveal any significant overlap in the neural substrates of Event-based PM disruption across the patient groups.

definition.value: Voxel-based morphometry results showing regions of significant gray matter intensity decrease associated with Event-based prospective memory performance exclusive to AD.

value: Regions exclusively implicated in Event-based PM disruption in AD included the right orbitofrontal cortex, left hippocampus, bilateral middle temporal gyri and right temporal pole, extending posteriorly to the left superior parietal lobule, bilateral angular gyri, right precuneus, and left occipital pole.

definition.value: Voxel-based morphometry results showing regions of significant gray matter intensity decrease associated with Event-based prospective memory performance exclusive to bvFTD.

value: For bvFTD, regions exclusively in the temporal lobes, notably the bilateral hippocampi and left lateral temporal cortices, were implicated in Event-based PM disruption.

description.value: Participants completed three Time-based and three Event-based prospective memory tasks while engaged in a filler task involving viewing and describing humorous cartoons. The entire task took approximately 20 minutes.

spans.text: prospective memory task

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to execute intended actions after specified amounts of time or following specified events. Instructions were read aloud from a standard script; participants could use pencil and paper and a clock as external aids.

stimuli.value: Humorous cartoons, time cues, event cues including an alarm, pencil and paper, and a clock.
